decisions.title: Authorization boundary

options.label: Explicit public and protected routers
options.consequence: All node-local routes inherit authorization unless deliberately placed in the small public router.

options.label: Per-handler authorization
options.consequence: Every current and future handler must remember to opt in, leaving omission as an anonymous-data leak.

decisions.rationale: Deny-by-default routing makes the security boundary reviewable and future-safe.

decisions.title: Local authorization persistence

options.label: Migrated SQLite owner, handoff, and session records
options.consequence: Browser authorization and owner identity survive node restart and participate in atomic claims/revocations.

options.label: Process-local maps
options.consequence: Restart loses sessions and handoffs, and ownership/replay behavior cannot be transactionally enforced.

decisions.rationale: The accepted session lifetime and restart behavior require durable local state.

decisions.title: Browser handoff binding

options.label: HTTP-only pre-auth binding cookie plus atomic handoff claim
options.consequence: The callback URL alone is insufficient in another browser and one matching concurrent claimant wins.

options.label: Handoff UUID only
options.consequence: Anyone receiving the callback URL can complete the handoff in a different browser.

decisions.rationale: A browser-held secret binds the existing Hive handoff without exposing daemon credentials.

decisions.title: Owner lifecycle

options.label: First subject pins; different subjects reject; disconnect retains owner
options.consequence: A disconnected node remains owned and cannot be claimed by another Hive user through ordinary OAuth.

options.label: Disconnect clears owner
options.consequence: Anyone who can reach a disconnected trusted-LAN node can race to become its new owner.

options.label: Different OAuth subject replaces owner
options.consequence: Normal login doubles as an ownership-transfer path without a separate high-risk confirmation.

decisions.rationale: The roadmap is single-owner and explicitly excludes an owner-transfer workflow.

decisions.title: Logout and disconnect API

options.label: Add browser-session logout; keep explicit Hive disconnect separate
options.consequence: UI logout revokes one browser while existing daemon-disconnect semantics remain available as a protected operation.

options.label: Reuse one logout operation for both
options.consequence: A routine browser logout stops sync and revokes every browser session.

decisions.rationale: The two operator intents have different revocation scopes and must remain visible.

decisions.title: Hive outage semantics

options.label: Authorize locally after session creation
options.consequence: Established local work continues through transport, timeout, refresh, and 5xx failures.

options.label: Revalidate every browser request with Hive
options.consequence: Hive availability becomes a dependency for all node-local operations.

decisions.rationale: Local availability is a first-release requirement and explicit disconnect remains the only intentional global revocation path.

decisions.title: Long-lived stream authentication

options.label: Browser cookie by default; route-scoped connection tokens for direct logs/diffs and proxy tokens for node-to-node HTTP
options.consequence: Local browser streams share one boundary while existing remote log, diff, and proxy consumers remain available through narrowly scoped token audiences without anonymous fallback.

options.label: Require browser cookie on every stream and proxy route without exception
options.consequence: Existing Hive-issued remote log, diff, and node-proxy consumers can no longer connect to the node.

options.label: Use one generic token predicate for every alternative route
options.consequence: A connection token can cross into node-proxy operations or a proxy token can cross into direct execution streams, widening each credential beyond its intended audience.

options.label: Leave streams anonymous when no token is supplied
options.consequence: Unauthenticated LAN clients retain raw execution, diff, and terminal access.

decisions.rationale: Preserve the production remote-diff and node-proxy paths while closing the ignored-token hole and enforcing the existing `connection` versus `node_proxy` audience split.

decisions.title: Frontend bootstrap

options.label: Minimal public auth state, then protected app bootstrap
options.consequence: Fresh browsers render login without receiving configuration or starting protected live connections.

options.label: Keep `/api/info` public
options.consequence: Unauthenticated clients continue receiving node configuration and executor/environment information.

decisions.rationale: The login shell needs only authorization availability, not protected system data.

decisions.title: Session cookie policy

options.label: Five-year HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie without Secure
options.consequence: Sessions persist across browser restart on supported plain HTTP LAN deployments, with the documented plaintext risk.

options.label: Require Secure
options.consequence: Browsers on the explicitly supported HTTP deployment will not send the session cookie.

options.label: Short server expiry
options.consequence: The operator must periodically reauthenticate and Hive availability affects routine local continuity.

decisions.rationale: This exactly matches the accepted trusted-LAN and generous-session constraints.

obstacles.obstacle: The current router merges every API into one anonymous subtree and unknown API GETs can fall through to SPA HTML.
obstacles.countermeasure: Construct explicit public/protected routers, authenticate the protected subtree, and terminate unknown `/api/*` paths inside the API boundary.

obstacles.obstacle: WebSocket and SSE handlers currently upgrade or stream without a browser-session boundary; optional-token routes accept no token as local access; and task-attempt diff URLs carry a connection token that the server currently ignores.
obstacles.countermeasure: Authenticate before extraction/upgrade for every stream, remove anonymous fallback, validate `connection` tokens only on direct-log/direct-diff routes, validate distinct `node_proxy` tokens only on node-to-node HTTP routes, and reject every cross-audience attempt.

obstacles.obstacle: The existing handoff UUID is bearer-like and global auth polling authorizes every browser after daemon login.
obstacles.countermeasure: Bind each handoff to a secret HTTP-only browser cookie and return browser-specific local auth state from the presenting session.

obstacles.obstacle: Local pending handoffs have no timestamp and removal-before-I/O is not a durable atomic single-consumer contract.
obstacles.countermeasure: Persist exact expiry and state, conditionally claim matching pending rows, and make claimed/completed/failed rows non-replayable.

obstacles.obstacle: No browser-session schema or cookie exists, and daemon profile cache disappears on restart.
obstacles.countermeasure: Persist hash-only local sessions independent of profile cache and issue a long-lived opaque cookie with no server-time expiry check.

obstacles.obstacle: The node currently saves candidate credentials before profile lookup and persists no stable owner subject.
obstacles.countermeasure: Fetch candidate profile first, atomically pin/compare the owner, reject mismatches, and only then replace daemon credentials and mint a session.

obstacles.obstacle: Current navbar logout invokes global daemon logout, stops sync, and deletes credentials.
obstacles.countermeasure: Add a presenting-session revocation operation and update navbar state without calling the explicit disconnect path.

obstacles.obstacle: SQLite session revocation and file/Keychain credential deletion cannot share one transaction.
obstacles.countermeasure: Revoke all sessions transactionally first, then stop sync/delete credentials, return any deletion failure visibly, and retain the pinned owner.

obstacles.obstacle: Current login status depends on cached/remote Hive profile and restart during outage appears logged out.
obstacles.countermeasure: Derive browser authorization solely from durable local sessions and keep transport/refresh errors separate from explicit disconnect side effects.

obstacles.obstacle: OAuth changes can accidentally return candidate tokens in errors, redirects, debug logs, or frontend state.
obstacles.countermeasure: Keep redemption and profile lookup server-side, redact token-bearing errors, use opaque local cookies, and scan real-harness browser-visible surfaces with sentinel credentials.

decision_points.trigger: Execution reaches the additive SQLite migration task and requires explicit approval before applying an irreversible production schema migration.

assumptions.claim: Hive exposes a stable owner subject as `ProfileResponse.user_id` derived from the authenticated Hive user UUID.
The current node callback consumes a process-local handoff and saves Hive credentials server-side without a browser-specific session.
All current node APIs and node-local stream routers lack a browser-session middleware boundary.
assumptions.probe: Read crates/server/src/routes/mod.rs:43-88 plus the task, draft, attempt, execution, log, event, and terminal stream route modules on 2026-08-21.

assumptions.claim: Shared migrated SQLite test pools and a real served-router/Wiremock Hive harness exist for deterministic and real-seam tests.
The WAI 0.30.0 submitter, child tracker, and draft spec exist before promotion.
A real Hive deployment and non-loopback browser can be made available for feature-branch acceptance evidence.
assumptions.probe: Run TS7 against the feature-branch build before close.

questions.asked: Should the trusted-LAN node remain anonymously open or require per-browser Hive OAuth?
Should the first release enforce TLS, Secure cookies, CORS, or Origin policy?
